newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli army sources deny shelling Lebanese port.
newsitem.headline: Israeli army sources deny shelling Lebanese port.

text.p: Israeli military sources said on Monday the army was not behind the shelling of Lebanon's southern port city of Sidon in which six civilians were killed and 34 were wounded.

"The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) can say with full assurance it isn't IDF shelling of Sidon," one of the sources said. He said forces under the command of pro-Israeli militia leader Antoine Lahd were behind the attack.

Lahd is commander of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) in an Israeli-held occupation zone and of a militia force in the Jezzine area just outside the zone. Military sources said this was the group responsible.
"The people who shelled Sidon are from General Lahd's soldiers who are north of the security zone," a military source said.
"These are not people in the security zone. The SLA is backed by Israel whereas the people who fired are not backed by Israel," the source said.
Military sources said the shelling followed an increase in attacks on the Jezzine area.
The Israeli army said two Lebanese youths were killed and two wounded hours earlier when an explosive device blew up a vehicle in the Jezzine area.
The army said Hizbollah, the Iranian-backed "Party of God", carried out the attack.
Security sources in Lebanon said some of the 34 wounded civilians were seriously hurt in the three rounds of shelling on Sidon.
Israel and its SLA allies patrol a 15 km (nine mile) deep border zone set up inside Lebanon with the declared aim of preventing guerrilla attacks on Israel's northern border.
